verses: With long and tapering rods, You angle in the Ch'i. I think of you, dear friends, Here far removed from Wei.
Ch'uan-yuan upon the left, Ch'i on the right I view. But married far away, To home I bade adieu.
Those streams, this on the right, That on the left, appear. The laugh that shows your teeth, Your tinkling gems, I hear.
I watch the cedar oars On Ch'i, and boats of pine. O might I travel there, And soothe this heart of mine!
